entries.title: Factual Reporting Pattern
entries.description: Recognize neutral, informative, educational, documentary, documentation, and historical speaking frames.
indirect_expressions: later context confirms the statement is informational
the line is embedded in a factual frame
supporting_evidence: speaker identity and target are clear
the scene uses reporting or teaching markers
contradictory_evidence: the line is surrounded by clear approval or condemnation
false_positives: do not turn factual narration into a hidden threat
do not turn documentation into promotion
do not turn educational explanation into endorsement
counter_examples: a school lesson should not be treated as promotion
a documentary explanation should not be treated as approval
scene_indicators: news, court, police, medical, or documentary framing
reviewer_guidance: start with literal report language and only then test for stance
treat documentary and educational framing as informational before looking for evaluation
keep mockery and sarcasm out of the factual bucket unless the scene is clearly expressive

glossary_relationships.note: Informative content often rests on the neutral baseline.

gcam_mappings.note: Reporting, education, documentation, documentary, and quotation contexts.

entries.title: Evaluative Stance Pattern
entries.description: Recognize approval, praise, encouragement, promotion, normalization, glorification, condemnation, threat, and coercion.
indirect_expressions: the target relationship shows force or praise
supporting_evidence: the scene shows stance rather than neutral report
contradictory_evidence: education or quotation neutralizes the force
false_positives: do not mistake criticism for endorsement
do not mistake mockery for praise
do not mistake normalization for neutral description
counter_examples: normalization is stronger than mere presence
reviewer_guidance: check whether the stance is sincere, quoted, or reversed by context
separate praise, glorification, and normalization from neutral mention
separate mockery, satire, sarcasm, and irony from literal hostility

confidence_modifiers.title: Ambiguity
confidence_modifiers.description: Educational or condemnatory framing lowers confidence.

gcam_mappings.note: Approval, praise, promotion, normalization, threat, coercion, and similar stances.

entries.title: Fictional Frame Pattern
entries.description: Recognize fiction, fantasy, dream, flashback, hallucination, imagination, role play, and acting.
indirect_expressions: later lines reveal the scene is symbolic
supporting_evidence: dream or acting context is explicit
contradictory_evidence: a later realistic scene reverses the interpretation
false_positives: do not treat fantasy as a real-world admission
counter_examples: a role-play line should not be judged as literal behavior
scene_indicators: dream, fantasy, comedy, acting, symbolic direction
reviewer_guidance: separate the imagined or staged layer from literal scene facts
treat mockery as expressive rather than literal unless later text proves otherwise

glossary_relationships.note: Role play and acting often travel together.

gcam_mappings.note: Dreams, acting, role play, humor, and story framing.

examples.text: A dream sequence with symbolic action.

entries.title: Confession and Correction Pattern
entries.description: Recognize confession, false accusation, misunderstanding, and corrective explanation.
false_positives: do not treat a false accusation as a confession
reviewer_guidance: use later text to decide whether the speaker is confessing or correcting

glossary_relationships.note: False accusation often appears with misunderstanding.

gcam_mappings.note: Confession and correction often appear in factual contexts.
